title: dynamic-tenant-weighting-and-utilization-delta-reporter
author: Maya Thompson
release_notes: Adds dynamic tenant weighting for Dedicated allocator and new utilization_delta metrics for fleet reporting. Backwards-compatible rollout under feature flag.
description:
Summary: Introduce dynamic tenant weighting in the Dedicated capacity allocator and a compact utilization_delta reporter that emits per-tenant utilization change metrics to the telemetry pipeline.

Motivation: current static tenant weights make burst fairness and throughput guarantees brittle when tenant workloads shift rapidly (e.g., short-lived traffic spikes or background batch imports). We need a way to adapt allocations quickly without causing oscillation or violating throughput SLAs, and to produce a lightweight delta metric stream for rolling-window reporting and chargeback.

Design: 1) Dynamic weighting controller: a new controller in the dedicated allocator that computes an 'effective_weight' per tenant every control interval by combining configured reservation (static), recent short-window utilization, and an inertia term to damp oscillation. The formula used: effective_weight = max(static_reservation, clamp(static_reservation * (1 + alpha * short_util_delta), min_factor, max_factor)) where alpha defaults to 0.4 and short_util_delta is the fractional change in utilization over the last 30s window. The controller runs asynchronously and updates the tenant weight in the allocator without requiring a global restart.

2) Utilization-delta reporter: emits compact metrics: tenant.utilization.delta (percent change), tenant.effective_weight (float), tenant.burst_reconcile.count (int) with 10s granularity. The reporter intentionally avoids full histogram payloads to reduce cardinality and egress cost.

3) Burst reconciliation loop: when short_util_delta > threshold (0.25 by default) for more than two consecutive intervals, the allocator triggers a bounded 'burst_reconcile' that makes ephemeral burst tokens available to the tenant up to a tenant-specific budget. Tokens decay over a configurable window.

Implementation highlights:
- New package: dedicated/control/dynamic_weighting.go (controller + integration tests)
- Add a lightweight encoder for delta metrics in telemetry/compact_encoder.go
- Add e2e scenario harness for short spike -> weight adjust -> throttle avoidance in test/perf/dedicated_weight_e2e.test
- Feature flag: --enable-dynamic-tenant-weighting (off by default in release builds)

Rollout plan:
1) Merge behind feature flag.
2) Deploy to canary pool (slo-canary-1) and enable for a small set of non-critical tenants.
3) Monitor tenant.utilization.delta and tenant.effective_weight and gate on no more than 1.5x increase in tail latency over 5m per tenant.
4) Gradually widen the cohort if metrics are stable.

Backwards compatibility: The change is opt-in; if the flag is off the allocator behavior is unchanged. Metrics names are additive only.

Testing:
- Unit tests for controller logic with deterministic inputs and mocked clock.
- Integration test that simulates changing workload curves and validates the effective_weight bounds and no negative allocations.
- e2e load test on perf-canary showed 12% reduction in throttled requests for short spikes (30s) at the cost of 3% higher average GPU utilization in test harness.

Related: refers to ENG-2148 (autoscaling policy gaps) and ENG-2183 (telemetry cost reduction).

Notes:
- This PR optimizes dedicated capacity responsiveness to short-duration spikes while keeping long-term throughput guarantees enforced by static reservations.
- Feature flagged and covered by tests; recommend gradual rollout and close monitoring of tenant_tail_latency alerts in the first 48 hours after enabling per-tenant.
